messages:
Sam (support): Hey team, escalating a customer issue hitting embeddings route — they get a dimension mismatch error intermittently and also reported a billing spike yesterday. Need help with root cause and quick mitigations. Customer claim: some requests return 1024-dim vectors while others return 1536, and batching/throughput seems to correlate.

Irene L (eng-ml): Hmm. Do we know which model variant they're calling? Different quant/variant combos can change output dims if someone accidentally routes between models. Also possible malformed request metadata.

Sam (support): They are calling /v1/embeddings with model "open-embed-1" (as listed in their dashboard). We saw their app toggles a feature flag and then traffic shifts. Sample error from client: `{"error":"dimension mismatch: got 1536, expected 1024"}`. They pasted a trace id: trace=tr_8a7f3b9c.

Theo (observability): I pulled trace tr_8a7f3b9c — routing log shows two backend instances: embed-v1-1024 and embed-v2-1536. That suggests smart-routing picked a different variant mid-flight. Policy was "latency-prefer" for them.

Maya (SRE): If routing switches variant, batch compatibility might break. Our batching layer requires same vector shape for a batch. If one request is queued expecting 1024 and another 1536, the server should reject, but maybe we're falling back to per-request mode and returning a different shape. Any batching config in their request headers?

Sam (support): Customer sent this header in repro: `X-Client-Flags: feature_x=on;enable_fast_embed` and their SDK sets `Prefer: prefer-batching=auto`. They said issue happens under load > 300rps.

Irene L (eng-ml): Likely sequence: traffic spikes -> autoscaler spins new variant (maybe higher-accuracy 1536-dim) -> smart router routes some requests to new variant -> our batcher groups heterogeneous shapes -> processing code raises mismatch or falls back. We should confirm batcher logs and rejection metrics.

Theo (observability): I ran a per-request latency breakdown for that trace id. Relevant spans (flattened):
```
accept_time_ms: 0
queue_ms: 24
batching_wait_ms: 65
proc_kernel_ms: 112
kv_cache_ms: 18
postprocess_ms: 9
response_send_ms: 7
```
And an adjacent request (same 2s window) shows `proc_kernel_ms: 210` and `batching_wait_ms: 4` — pattern matches some requests got batched badly and slower kernel time suggests a different model variant.
```
trace link: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/tr_8a7f3b9c (internal only)
```

Maya (SRE): We should check `embeddings.route` logs around that timestamp for `batch_mismatch` or `batch_reject` flags. Also check autoscale events: I see a scale up at 2025-10-21T01:12:47Z for model embed-v2-1536.

Irene L (eng-ml): Quick mitigation: pin the customer's routing policy to "model-version" (force embed-v1-1024) or disable smart-routing for their account until we patch. We can also change their SDK to `Prefer: prefer-batching=off` to avoid mixed batches.

Sam (support): Customer asked for repro steps. Can we give them a simple curl that reproduces the mismatch? They also want steps to gather traces/headers for us.

Theo (observability): Repro curl (what to run from their app):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Prefer: prefer-batching=auto" \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":["short text","another text"]}'
```
Add `-H "X-Request-ID: <unique>"` to correlate with traces. Ask them to send us the X-Request-ID and timestamp. Also request `X-Client-Flags` header if present.

Irene L (eng-ml): Another repro script to hammer concurrency (Python) — looping with 400 concurrent workers with mixed feature flag header tends to surface it. Provide this with a note to run against staging first.

Maya (SRE): Observability checklist to send them:
- Include X-Request-ID in failing requests.
- Capture the response body and full error JSON.
- Collect SDK version and the exact model name returned in `model` field from successful responses.
- Note time window and any feature flag flips.

Sam (support): Billing spike portion — customer says they got charged for double-embedding units during the incident window. Could that be caused by retries when batch fails?

Irene L (eng-ml): Yes, if the SDK retries on batch failure and the server then processes a fallback per-request, they could double-count. Need to inspect the retry logs and client-side retry policy. Also check `billing.events` for duplicate request_ids.

Theo (observability): I pulled a sample: request_id 0a1b2c received retry header `x-retry-of: 0a1b2c` and two successful embeddings issued to different model variants; both were billed. We should treat retries that hit different model variants as duplicates and credit them.

Maya (SRE): Action items:
- (P0) Pin customer's routing to model-version and disable smart-routing for them — support can do temporary policy toggle.
- (P1) Update customer SDK guidance to set `Prefer: prefer-batching=off` or ensure consistent model pinning.
- (P1) Observability: add a dashboard panel for `batch_shape_variance` and `batch_reject_rate` per-account.
- (P2) Billing: run a query for duplicate billing events for customer_id and issue credit if confirmed.

Sam (support): I'll communicate temporary pin and ask them to run repro curl with X-Request-ID. Also will open a billing ticket.

Irene L (eng-ml): Longer-term fix ideas: stronger invariants at the router to avoid mixing variants in a queue, and a guard that returns a clear `400 batch shape mismatch` instead of silently falling back. Add unit test in batcher for mixed-shape detection.

Theo (observability): I'll add a quick dashboard tile and a trace link snippet to the support playbook. For now, to debug future cases tell customers to capture both `trace_id` and `x-request-id` and share console link.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: PR #4021 (batcher: explicit shape-check + metric) scheduled to deploy to canary in 15m :rocket:

Maya (SRE): Nice. Once canary is up we can run a synthetic load test to reproduce and validate the fix.

Sam (support): Thanks all — I'll update the customer and attach repro steps and the mitigation (pin + prefer-batching off). Will follow up once billing has an answer. :thumbsup:

Irene L (eng-ml): If customer pushes to roll-forward we should ensure the migration plan includes a background warm-up that keeps batch shapes consistent.

Sam (support): Logged follow-ups: SUP-99824 (esc), BILL-4521 (billing audit), ENG-1217 (batcher fix). Closing loop here once billing credit is confirmed.
